OPERATIONAL NOTE, NOT A MISSED CYCLE: this run's container was cloned from a stale point in the repo's git history (through the 2026-09-18 20:09 commit only), 15 commits behind the true tip of origin/main at session start. origin/main already contained proper individual commits for every 2026-09-19 through 2026-09-23 cycle, including real trades (9/21 USO/AMD trims and an MSFT add; 9/22 META initiation) -- those cycles' git pushes had succeeded; nothing was lost. This only surfaced when this run's own `git push` was rejected as a non-fast-forward update and `git fetch origin main` revealed the missing commits. Before discovering the true cause, this run had independently reconstructed the same 9/19-9/23 data from the live dashboard artifact's embedded JSON (a safeguard built into the Artifact tool's publish step, which refuses a publish that doesn't account for a newer unseen version) and briefly drafted a status.json note incorrectly attributing the gap to 'silent git push failures' by prior runs -- that draft was never pushed and has been corrected here. The final commit for this run is a proper two-parent merge of origin/main (the authoritative history) with this run's own two 9/24 trades, so no duplicate or fabricated history entries were introduced into data/transactions.json, data/history.json, or data/research_log.json. RECOMMENDATION: investigate why this session's container was provisioned from a stale ref instead of the true current HEAD of main -- e.g. a caching layer on repo clone, or a race between this session's start and a still-in-flight push from the prior cycle.
